title: Problem
description: One Elite Code practice problem. A problem is either a classic single-prompt coding problem (type "standard", exactly one stage) or a multi-stage interview simulation (type "simulation", 3-5 stages) where each stage extends the previous requirement. Solutions and tests are Python 3.14.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema file, for editor autocompletion. Ignored by the app.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the problem format this file follows. Must be exactly 1 for the current format.

id.description: Globally unique, stable identifier. Lowercase kebab-case. Also used as the file name (<id>.json).

title.description: Human-readable title shown in the problem list.

type.description: "standard": one prompt, one stage. "simulation": an interview that evolves through 3-5 stages; the solver only sees the current stage and must keep earlier stages passing.

difficulty.description: Overall difficulty for a mid-to-senior engineer. For simulations, rate the final stage.

tags.description: 1-5 topic tags from the fixed vocabulary, most important first. Used for filtering and weakest-topic analytics.

summary.description: One or two plain-text sentences (no Markdown) shown in the problem list. Must not reveal the solution approach or future simulation stages.
examples: Merge all overlapping time ranges in a calendar export.

starterCode.description: Python code the editor starts with: the function or class signature(s) the tests call, with a docstring and a `pass` or `raise NotImplementedError` body. Must NOT pass the tests. For simulations, starter code covers only stage 1.

packages.description: Third-party packages the solution or tests need. They are loaded before the code runs. Omit or leave empty for pure-Python problems (strongly preferred).

timeLimitSeconds.description: Wall-clock limit for one complete run of the solver's code plus every selected test, in the browser. Defaults to 5.

estimatedMinutes.description: Realistic time for a strong candidate to finish the whole problem (all stages), in minutes.

companies.description: Optional flavor: companies known to ask this kind of question. Free text.

topics.description: Optional flavor: free-form domain topics (e.g. "payments", "observability"). Unlike tags, not restricted to a vocabulary.

stages.description: Ordered stages. A standard problem has exactly one; a simulation has 3-5, revealed one at a time.

slug.title: Slug
slug.description: Lowercase kebab-case identifier: letters, digits and single hyphens, starting with a letter.

tag.title: Tag
tag.description: Topic tag from the fixed vocabulary.

packageName.title: PackageName
packageName.description: A package available to problems. Anything else is unavailable.

testName.title: TestName
testName.description: Test function name: starts with test_, then lowercase letters, digits and underscores. Unique across the whole problem.

testCase.title: TestCase
testCase.description: One test: Python source defining a single zero-argument function named exactly `name`. It passes if it returns without raising. Use plain `assert actual == expected` statements.

description.description: Optional one-line description of what the test checks, shown to the solver when the test is visible or fails.
examples: Touching intervals [1,2] and [2,3] merge into one.

code.description: Python source: `def <name>():` followed by an indented body. May start with imports. Runs after the solver's code in the same namespace, so it can call the solver's functions and classes directly.

hint.title: Hint
hint.description: A progressive hint (Markdown). The first nudges, the last nearly gives the approach away, but no hint contains full code.

code.description: Complete, runnable Python. For simulations it is cumulative: the whole program as it should look at the end of this stage, passing this stage's tests and every earlier stage's tests.

explanation.description: Markdown walkthrough of the approach, why it is correct, and (for simulations) what had to be refactored from the previous stage.

timeComplexity.description: Big-O time of the key operations, with variables defined.
examples: O(n log n) for n intervals

spaceComplexity.description: Big-O extra space, with variables defined.

stage.title: Stage
stage.description: One step of a problem. Standard problems have a single stage holding the whole prompt.

id.description: Stage identifier, unique within the problem.

requirement.description: Markdown prompt for this stage, written as the interviewer speaking. Defines every function/class/method signature the tests call, input/output formats, and the rules. Include at least one worked example.

visibleTests.description: Tests the solver can read and run with Run. Cover the worked examples and one or two simple edge cases.

hiddenTests.description: Tests only run on Submit. Cover edge cases, scale within the time limit, and shortcuts a naive solution would take.

hints.description: 2-3 ordered hints, revealed one at a time.
